transcript.dialogue: Hey, I'm Jordan. Honestly I'm mostly just here because my friends dared me to wear this blue jacket on camera, but what about you—how'd you end up in this noise box?
I keep a lighthouse. The gulls don't care much for arcade music. Do you think that machine is ever actually winning, or just lying?
I'm voting for lying. Definitely lying. Wait, you actually live in a lighthouse? That's... well, that's way less boring than what I do.
It's mostly damp. What is it that you do, Jordan, besides wear the blue dare jacket?
I fix things that people break, mostly old bikes and stuff. But honestly? I want to see this lighthouse now. Is it actually as quiet as it sounds?
It is quiet enough that you can hear the rust on the hinges. Do you know anything about fixing foghorns? One of mine has been making a wet coughing sound.
A wet coughing foghorn? Alright, challenge accepted. I'll fix your horn if you let me climb to the top before the lights go out.
Deal. My bus leaves in five minutes anyway. Here's my card—don't lose it to the gulls.
I won't. Text you when I've got my toolbox ready. See you, Juniper.
See you, Jordan. Bring a wrench that believes in ghosts.

A lighthouse! Oh, you are living my absolute Gothic romance fantasy. When the skies open up, I do cardamom brioche buns that puff up like little golden pillows. Do you actually bake out there, or just watch the waves rage?
